clue.text: Studied how to undo Bolivar's legacy?

definitions.meaning: studied in the sense of intentional, done on purpose
Simón Bolívar liberated much of South America, so undoing his work would be to reverse that liberation

explanation.surface: A historian ponders how one might reverse the achievements of Simón Bolívar.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: Bolívar liberated, so to undo his legacy is to 'de-liberate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something studied is done intentionally and with care, which is a deliberate act.

clue.text: From the Caribbean party, taking small jug

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
mini means small
a can is a vessel for liquid, like a jug

explanation.surface: Someone at a Caribbean party is carrying a little jug.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for the Caribbean island nation of Dominica or the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: What chap rising about one may have had?

definitions.text: What chap rising about one may have had?

indicators.note: about means the reversed name goes around the next piece
in a down entry, rising means the name is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Neil is a man's name, a chap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a man getting up late might have enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NEIL into LIEN, and 'about' puts I inside it. The whole clue also defines: a man getting up late has had a lie-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises late has stayed in bed longer than usual, a lazy morning.

clue.text: Worry over article and report not in? Be stoical!

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: to worry at something, as a dog does, is to bite it
the is the definite article

indicators.note: not means the following word is taken away

parts.note: a bulletin is a news report
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fretting about a news item that failed to arrive, someone is told to keep calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes IN from BULLETIN to leave BULLET.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to face something unpleasant with stoic courage, from biting a bullet during surgery.

clue.text: Lozenge given by extremely rash old doctor's no good

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of the word rash

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
US is crossword shorthand for useless, no good

explanation.surface: A medicinal lozenge prescribed by a careless old doctor turns out useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'rash' give RH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a diamond shape, which in geometry is an equilateral parallelogram.

clue.text: Short speech in case is most exaggerated

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: talk is speech
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A brief address in a court case turns out to be the most overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated one, so the superlative means the most exaggerated.

clue.text: Prejudice American leader's given into twice

indicators.note: given into means the letter is put inside the word for twice

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word American

explanation.surface: An American head of state twice yields to prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a synonym of prejudice, an unfair leaning for or against something.

clue.text: How Britain's colonies appeared on maps to be fighting fit?

definitions.text: How Britain's colonies appeared on maps
definitions.meaning: the British Empire was traditionally coloured pink on world maps

explanation.surface: Old imperial maps and robust health are linked by a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: On old maps the British Empire was shown in pink, and 'in the pink' is a British idiom for being very healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in excellent health, and literally describes territory coloured pink.

clue.text: People having digs see this column as least decipherable

definitions.text: People having digs see this column

indicators.note: decipherable suggests the letters can be worked out into another order

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find an inscribed column very hard to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People having digs' sounds like lodgers but means archaeologists, who excavate inscribed stone pillars.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright inscribed stone slab or pillar found by archaeologists on excavations.

clue.text: Making comeback in sport, seamer is best in field

indicators.note: Making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fast bowler returning to cricket proves the finest player on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'is', but a noun cannot stand in for 'is best in field', so 'is' is a link. 'Making comeback' reverses ORTSEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master, someone outstanding in their area of expertise.

clue.text: Boy about to barge into old girl, a lager lout

indicators.note: barging into means pushing inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: late means former, old

indicators.note: about means the name is turned round

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad shoves past an elderly lady while drunk on lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the boy's name and 'to barge into' pushes it inside the word for old. 'old girl' looks like one unit, but 'girl' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves in a boisterous, hard-drinking laddish way.

clue.text: Tortured soul with bad heroin bringing disgrace

indicators.note: tortured means twisted, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A tormented addict's bad heroin habit brings shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct that is shameful brings disgrace on someone.

clue.text: Goal so defective, players found?

definitions.meaning: a goal so faulty it has ...

explanation.surface: A football goal lacking its netting leaves the players stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer describes a broken goal; as one it is a group of nine players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine musicians, a group of players.

clue.text: Drinks cupbearer shortly brought to a Middle Eastern town

parts.note: beers are drinks

indicators.note: shortly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods

explanation.surface: Drinks are carried by a servant to a town in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Beersheba is a city in the Negev desert of southern Israel.

clue.text: I like to exchange views on Tess, Victorian novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Someone keen to discuss Hardy's Victorian novel about Tess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Tess of the d'Urbervilles, but 'novel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who enjoys talk and sharing opinions might say this of themselves.

clue.text: What may be headed for correspondent?

definitions.text: What may be headed for correspondent?

parts.words: What may be headed for correspondent?
parts.note: stationery for letter writers often carries a printed address at the top, so it is headed

explanation.surface: Something that may be destined for a letter writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed' suggests travelling towards someone, but means having a printed letterhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is often headed with an address, and is used by those who correspond.

clue.text: Document proving ownership? Criminal deleted it

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook erased the record that proved who owned the property.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document showing who holds title to a property.

clue.text: Little in prospect? That's plain

definitions.meaning: very little in view, nothing much to see

explanation.surface: A dull view and a plain face are described the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unattractive, and literally describes a view with little worth seeing.

clue.text: Artist producing animal paintings, horses primarily

parts.note: a hog is a pig, an animal
art is paintings collectively

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the word horses

explanation.surface: A painter turns out pictures of animals, mostly horses.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was an English painter known for satirical series like A Rake's Progress.

clue.text: Last longer than old hat and dress

parts.note: out means out of fashion, old hat
wear is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: A tired hat and frock outlive their usefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to outlast it in use.

clue.text: Trajectory described by spinner as excellent

indicators.note: described by means the second piece is attached to and follows the first

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
flight is the path a ball takes, its trajectory

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praises the arc of a spin bowler's delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket, but it is a spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank, first-class or excellent.

clue.text: Neglected to give Billy Bunter another starter

indicators.note: another starter means the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, was mocked as Fatty

explanation.surface: A neglected boy is fed yet another first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a fat schoolboy from classic British children's stories; FATTY with T for F gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and worn, as something neglected becomes.

clue.text: Indian rhino standing in short grass

definitions.note: rhino is old slang for money

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
up means standing, on one's feet

explanation.surface: An Indian rhinoceros stands in a field of cropped grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' looks like the animal but is slang for money; 'short' cuts REED to REE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is India's currency, and rhino is old British slang for money.

clue.text: Sport, say, on a lake after rainfall

parts.note: sport is an example of play

explanation.surface: Playing games on a lake swollen by rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A playa is a desert basin that becomes a shallow lake after rain.

clue.text: Person trying to secure front of pub is old barman

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a taster is someone who tries food or drink

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the word pub

explanation.surface: A taster tries to get hold of a pub, a former bartender.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster was historically someone who drew beer from the tap in an inn.

clue.text: Became excited about initially royal welcome

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around another
excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled
initially takes the first letter of the word royal

explanation.surface: Someone grew excited about a royal welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges BECAME to EMBACE, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or person is to welcome them warmly.

clue.text: Bowl found in fifteenth century house

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to ... a batsman is to bowl a ball pitching at their feet
the royal house that fought the Wars of the Roses with Lancaster

explanation.surface: A bowl unearthed in an old fifteenth-century home.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batsman's feet; the House of York held the English throne in the 1400s.
explanation.definitionFit: To york is a cricket verb for bowling a yorker, and York was a royal house.

clue.text: Supervisor given cards following attack

indicators.note: following means the cards piece comes after the attack piece

parts.note: a charge is an attack
a hand is the set of cards held by a player

explanation.surface: A foreman is handed cards after an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a worker in charge of others, a foreman or supervisor.
